I’m sitting in my dark room feeling so incredibly bitter and jealous. I want to tell everyone she barely coded a line, but I also feel like a pathetic, petty loser for letting this eat me alive.

I saw the WhatsApp group updates about the class grading curve for our DBMS midterms. My best friend topped the class again with a perfect score while I barely scraped by the pass mark. I had to type 'so proud of you bro!!!' with shaking hands while literally crying on my keyboard. I feel like this disgusting, toxic person because I secretly wanted him to fail just so I wouldn't feel so incredibly small next to him. How do I stop this burning envy from ruining the only good friendship I have left?

Everyone in my coding batch is getting these crazy summer internship offers and posting their fancy welcome kits on LinkedIn. I spent my whole weekend failing LeetCode easy problems and staring at my empty inbox. I feel this toxic, bitter jealousy every time I open my phone, like my chest is physically burning. It’s like they all got the manual on how to succeed and my copy was blank. I’m starting to hate everyone who is doing well, and I hate myself even more for being this bitter.

My roommate just bagged a 24 LPA offer at a product company, and everyone is putting up LinkedIn posts congratulating him. I’m sitting here with a 6.8 CGPA, unable to even clear the basic round of a service-based company's coding test. I literally had to lock myself in the washroom because my hands were shaking seeing his WhatsApp status. I want to feel happy for him, he's my friend, but honestly? It feels like acid in my stomach. Why does it feel like his success has completely sealed my fate as a failure?

Sharma uncle called my dad today to brag about how his son got a 9.5 CGPA in the midterms and already has an internship offer. Now my dad is giving me silent treatment, just staring at my 7.1 report card like I ruined his life. I’m so incredibly bitter. I’ve been coding until 3 AM every day, but all my effort feels invisible compared to his kid's perfect life. I hate how much I resent him right now, but I can't help feeling like his existence is just a constant stick to beat me with.

The professor picked Rahul to lead the research project today, even though I did 80% of the groundwork in the lab work last semester. He’s charismatic, speaks well, and everyone loves him, while I just sit in the corner grinding away. Seeing him get all the praise and the recommendation letter makes me feel sick to my stomach. I'm so jealous of how easy everything is for him, and I hate myself for being this petty.

Every time the WhatsApp group notification pings, it’s another 'Congratulations to X for securing an internship at Y!' post. I literally have to mute the group because my chest gets so tight and I feel this toxic wave of envy. I’m happy they are succeeding, but why does it feel like the world is moving forward in hyper-speed while I’m stuck in cement? I can't even get past the resume screening stage.

My lab partner balances a relationship, goes out every weekend, and still finishes his DSA coding assignments in like twenty minutes. Meanwhile, I spent my entire weekend crying over a single backtracking problem and still got a compilation error in the lab test today. I look at his life and I feel this burning, ugly jealousy. Why does he get to have a social life and academic genius, while I'm sacrificing my mental health just to barely pass?

My roommate just got placed at a massive product company with an 18 LPA package. He literally started coding after me, and here I am, still getting 'Compilation Error' on basic Linked List questions in mock tests. I couldn't even sleep last night; every time I closed my eyes, I kept thinking about his LinkedIn post and my dad calling to ask 'aur tumhara kya chal raha hai?'. I feel this disgusting, burning knot in my chest because I want to be happy for him, but honestly, I just feel sick to my stomach and furious that he made it look so easy while I'm drowning.

Grades came out today and she got a 9.4 CGPA. I worked my absolute ass off, stayed up till 3 AM every night doing those stupid lab files, and still ended up with a 6.8. When she complained about her 'bad grade' in the WhatsApp group, I felt this wave of pure hatred. I hate how effortless everything is for her, and I hate myself even more for being so bitter about my own best friend’s success.

My cousin just cracked an off-campus role at some MNC and my mom won't stop talking about it. Every single call starts with 'usne toh clear kar liya, tumhara DSA kab khatam hoga?'. I felt so angry that I hung up on her and blocked my cousin's updates on Instagram. I feel like this toxic, jealous loser who can't stand seeing my own family succeed, but I'm just so tired of being the disappointment of the house.

In today's project evaluation, the professor praised my teammate for 'outstanding leadership' and basically ignored all the backend work I spent two weeks debugging. Everyone is congratulating him on the Discord server, and I’m just sitting here in the dark, crying because I want his spotlight so badly. I feel so invisible and incredibly jealous that he gets the applause while I do the actual heavy lifting.

My batchmate got a top rank in the coaching mock test and his photo is all over the main banner today. My dad took out a massive loan for this JEE prep, and seeing that guy's face just makes me feel physically sick with envy. He has private tutors and a peaceful house, while I'm sharing a room with three people and trying to study under a street light when the power cuts out. Why does he get the success and the resources, while I get nothing but guilt and anxiety?

I hate myself for this, but I literally felt sick when Rahul got that 35 LPA package from Atlassian. We literally lived in the same hostel room, cracked the same DSA questions, and did all our labs together, but his CGPA is 8.9 and mine is 7.2. Now my dad is calling me everyday asking why I can't just clear the coding rounds like he did. I can't even look at Rahul's face without feeling this absolute, toxic burn in my chest. I'm happy for him but it's killing me that I'm left behind in this stupid rat race.

Everyone on our college WhatsApp group is posting about their summer internships at FAANG and I'm just sitting here with a stupid unpaid local QA internship. I saw Pooja's post about her Google offer and I literally closed my phone and cried for an hour. I worked just as hard as her, didn't sleep during midterms, and yet she gets the glory and I get nothing. It feels like she took the life that was supposed to be mine, and now I just feel this deep, ugly resentment every time I see her name.

My cousin just cleared the UPSC prelims on his first attempt and now my entire family won't stop talking about him. During the family dinner yesterday, my uncle literally looked at my mediocre 7.5 CGPA sheet and asked if I'm even trying to secure a future. I feel so incredibly small and bitter towards my cousin, even though he didn't do anything wrong. I hate how his success makes me feel like an absolute waste of space in my own home.

My lab partner got shortlisted for the MS program in Europe and I didn't even pass the first screening round despite having the exact same project work. I have to sit next to him in the DSA lab every single day and pretend to be happy while he talks about visa processing and housing. I can feel this ugly, hot anger rising in my throat every time he opens his mouth, and then I feel disgusting for being such a horrible friend. Why does it have to be so easy for him while I'm struggling just to clear my backlogs?

I saw the class grading curve today and realized my roommate topped the batch while I barely scraped a passing grade. We studied the exact same notes, stayed up the same nights, but he just gets it effortlessly while I have to kill myself just to understand basic pointers. Now he's offering to 'help' me study, and it feels like a slap in the face. I feel so incredibly jealous and stupid, like my brain is just physically inferior and I'll always be his shadow.

My roommate just got a 45 LPA off-campus offer at some high-frequency trading firm, and I’m literally rotting here with my 7.2 CGPA and three active backlogs. We used to copy each other's DSA assignments, but now he doesn't even look at me when he talks, and his parents sent sweets to our room. I feel this sick, hot knot in my stomach every time he opens his laptop; I hate how much I despise his success when I should be happy for him.

My cousin got into an Ivy League for his MS while I couldn't even clear the cutoff for local state colleges, and now my dad keeps showing me his LinkedIn posts during dinner. I had to mute our family WhatsApp group because every single message is just praising him and subtly reminding me of my failures. I literally feel physically sick seeing his face, and I can't stop thinking that everyone views me as the defective child of the family.

My lab partner got shortlisted for the final round of Google interviews, and I got rejected in the first resume screening even though we have the exact same resume and projects. I pretended to congratulate her and even helped her prep for system design, but inside, I wanted her to fail so badly just so we'd be equal again. I feel like such an evil, disgusting person for wishing bad on a friend, but the jealousy is literally eating me alive.

I saw my ex-girlfriend posting photos with her new batchmate from her MBA college, and he looks like everything I'm not—secure, successful, and already placed at a top consulting firm. Here I am, still stuck preparing for GATE for the third time in my dingy room, feeling this toxic rage and envy that she upgraded so easily while I'm completely stagnant. I can't sleep because I keep comparing my broke, stressed-out self to his polished life.

During today's DSA coding lab, the professor publicly praised this one guy for writing a highly optimized O(log N) solution, while I couldn't even get my basic brute-force code to compile. Everyone was crowding around his desk asking for tips, and I just sat there staring at my red compilation errors, feeling this bitter, toxic envy. I wanted to smash my laptop because it feels like no matter how many hours I grind on LeetCode, some people are just naturally wired to be better than me.

My roommate just cleared the second round of his off-campus interview at Google while I'm struggling to get a single OA link. He acts all humble, like 'oh I just got lucky with the DSA tree question,' but I can't even look at him without my stomach churning. We literally studied the same LeetCode sheet, so why am I stuck with two backlogs while he's discussing CTC packages on the phone with his dad?

My cousin just got a 18 LPA package at a fintech firm and my dad literally spent the entire dinner talking about how 'focused' he is. I got a 6.8 CGPA this semester, and now every family call feels like an interrogation where I have to justify why I'm not a genius like him. I honestly hate my cousin so much right now, even though he didn't do anything wrong, and it makes me feel like an absolute monster.

My lab partner just posted on LinkedIn about getting a research fellowship under our HOD. I was the one who did 80% of the heavy lifting in our WebDev project last month, but because she is great at public speaking and networking, she got the recommendation letter. I'm sitting in my room, staring at her post with this toxic heat in my chest, feeling so incredibly small and bitter.

Everyone in my college WhatsApp group is talking about their summer internships, and here I am, still searching for an unpaid role just to save my resume from being blank. When I see my classmates sharing their onboarding kits and laptop pictures, I feel this sickening mix of envy and panic. I literally had to mute the group because seeing their success makes me feel like a complete waste of space.

My best friend from school just bought a new car with his placement bonus while I failed my third consecutive coding round today because of some stupid dynamic programming logic. We used to be equals, but now he's treating everyone to dinner and I'm calculating how to skip meals to save money. I can't help but feel this ugly, toxic jealousy toward him, and it's slowly destroying our friendship because I can't even bear to look at his messages anymore.
